method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the natives reached by AskWidget, CommonAskWidget, the widget base scripts and the DesktopWidget message path (per-row corpusCallSites list the scripts) and that the earlier contracts record only by name or not at all: the parent and child widget accessors, the keyboard focus request, the keyboard-only tutorial test and the two desktop message pool appenders. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish server behavior or widget content.

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/widget_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/world_master_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter and the return pushers.
framework.listOrder: Every registrar here builds the return list first and the argument list second. The wrapper call pushes the return list, the argument list, an adjustment of 0 from the zeroed EDI, the callback and a stack value, then installs the functor through 0x00CCCAD0. The wrapper stores the argument list at functor +0x14 and the return list at +0x24.
framework.receiverAdapter: Each invoke routine passes the receiver LuaControl to 0x009DA6CC with source type descriptor 0x01270B4C and its own target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback. A successful cast adds the stored adjustment from holder +0x0C and calls the member function pointer at holder +0x08 with ExecuteParameters on the stack, then returns true. The type descriptor names are .?AVWidgetBase@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@, .?AVDesktopWidget@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@, .?AVWorldMaster@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@ and .?AVLuaControl@GameEngine@Lua@Component@@.
framework.falseHolderResult: 0x00D19B70 calls the holder at 0x00D19D3B and tests AL at 0x00D19D3D. A zero result formats the literal at 0x0110F57C, Component::Lua::GameEngine::Functor::Execute, with the format at 0x0110F5AC and line number 0x71, pushes it through 0x00CF3360 and calls 0x00CF38A0, the same pair that reports the GetArguments_ failure.

executeParameters.+0x04: Engine handle. 0x00CC7510 loads the engine pointer from the handle and tail-calls 0x00CD7910, which returns engine +0x220. The callbacks read through that address.
executeParameters.+0x08: Lua thread object. _appendMessagePool passes it as the receiver of the yield request 0x00CD2860.
executeParameters.+0x0C: Receiver control identity, passed by address to the 0x0075B... workers.
executeParameters.+0x10: Argument container. Its dword at +0x04 points at the cell vector with first pointer at +0x04, end pointer at +0x08 and 16-byte cells whose tag byte is at +0x0C.
executeParameters.+0x1C: Return container, the receiver of the push routines.

framework.stateChain: A callback that works on widgets calls 0x00CC7510 with the engine handle, reads the dword at the returned address, reads the dword at +0x04 of that value and then the dword at +0x04 of that value. The workers 0x0075BA50, 0x0075BA90, 0x0075BAB0, 0x0075B9C0 and 0x0075B9E0 apply [ecx] of that last object as the context for 0x004D9910.

identityLookup.0x004D9910: Searches the tree at context +0x17804 through 0x0071D420 for the identity dword and returns the dword at +0x10 of the found node, or 0 when the search ends at the end node (0x004D9916..0x004D9963).
identityLookup.0x00CC7A50: Calls 0x00CD80F0 on the identity, then 0x00CD81D0 when it returns nonzero and 0x00CD8160 otherwise. A found record returns its first dword. A miss returns 0.
identityLookup.0x00CD8160: Returns 0 when the identity dword equals the dword at 0x0130C778, which holds 0xE0000000 in the image. Otherwise it looks the identity up in the container at engine +0x17C through 0x00D0A370.
identityLookup.0x004D6750: Returns the dword at +0x88 of its receiver, the identity of a widget object.
identityLookup.emptyIdentity: 0xC0000000 is the empty identity returned for a missing parent or child.

returnPushers.0x00748870: bool, built as a tag 2 value through 0x00583E30 and appended through 0x00584EE0
returnPushers.0x00748B30: LuaControl*. A null control pushes Nil, see manifests/desktop_native_call_contract.json framework.luaControlPush.

argumentReaders.0x005819A0: Reads cell tag 0, the int, and returns a pointer to the value stored through cell +0x08. A mismatched tag reaches 0x00CCA730 with the registry entry for the expected type and returns the static dword at 0x0133899C.
argumentReaders.0x0071CE70: Reads cell tag 3, the Utf8String. A mismatched tag reaches 0x00CCA730 and returns the static Utf8String at 0x0134B4C8.
argumentReaders.0x0071BB80: Reads cell tag 4 and casts a non-null control through 0x009DA6CC to the type descriptor 0x01270964, .?AVActorBase@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@. A failed cast or another tag reaches 0x00CCA730. A null control passes.
argumentReaders.0x00CCA730: Returns early to a write at address 0 when its receiver field at +0x08 is zero. Otherwise it builds a message, pushes it through 0x00CF3360 and calls 0x00CF38A0. If that call returns, the routine throws an object with vftable 0x00FA09D8 through 0x009D15C1. Whether 0x00CF38A0 returns is unknown.

framework.invalidParameterRoute: A cell-vector size check that fails calls 0x009D22B4 (calls at 0x0070756F in _getChildWidget and 0x00707893, 0x007078D6, 0x00707915 in the focus slot 0x00707870; the pool size checks in worker 0x006E8360 were not traced). The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.
framework.scriptBinding: Each row's scriptBinding names the class and script that xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json lists for the native. The _inl descriptor mapping was not traced.

rows.behavior: Reads the control identity at ExecuteParameters +0x0C and passes its address to 0x0075BA50 on the worker object. The worker resolves the identity to a widget object through 0x004D9910 and calls 0x00533ED0 on it. That routine returns the identity at +0x88 of the object held in the dword at widget +0xD8, or 0xC0000000 when +0xD8 is 0. Identity 0xC0000000 pushes Nil. Any other identity is resolved through 0x00CC7A50 and pushed as LuaControl*, which is Nil when the resolve returns null. The callback takes no argument and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads the engine handle at ExecuteParameters +0x04 and the identity at +0x0C, then walks the state chain and calls 0x0075BA50 with the identity address.
0x0075BA50 resolves the identity through 0x004D9910 and calls 0x00533ED0 on the result. No instruction tests the resolved object for null.
0x00533ED0 tests the dword at +0xD8 of its receiver. A nonzero value tail-calls 0x004D6750, which returns the dword at +0x88 of that object. Zero returns 0xC0000000.
Identity 0xC0000000 takes the Nil push at 0x0070747D. Any other identity is stored through 0x00CC9320, resolved through 0x00CC7A50 against the engine handle and pushed through 0x00748B30.
0x00CC7A50 returns 0 for an identity that no lookup finds, and 0x00CD8160 returns 0 for the identity equal to the dword at 0x0130C778. A null control is pushed as Nil.

The dword at widget +0xD8 holds the parent widget object. The native name and the Nil branch support it. No store to that field was traced, and _setParentWidget reaches 0x0075BA70 and 0x005393B0 without a traced store.
A receiver whose identity is absent from the 0x004D9910 tree makes 0x00533ED0 read address 0x000000D8. Whether the process survives that fault is unknown.

arguments.note: One-based child position. The callback passes it minus 1.

returns.handlerPush: 0x00748B30, or Nil for a null control

rows.behavior: Reads argument 0 as an int and passes it minus 1 with the control identity address to 0x0075BAB0. The worker resolves the widget through 0x004D9910 and calls 0x00537C10 with the zero-based index. A negative index and an index greater than the child count return 0xC0000000. Any other index reads the child pointer vector through 0x0052F7F0 and returns the identity of the child object. The index equal to the count fails the vector check in 0x0052F7F0 and throws std::out_of_range. A returned identity is resolved through 0x00CC7A50 and pushed as LuaControl*. Unlike _getParentWidget, this callback has no test for 0xC0000000 before the resolve. The callback requests no yield.

facts.claim: Argument 0 is read at index 0 through 0x005819A0 and decremented before the call to 0x0075BAB0.

0x00537C10 returns 0xC0000000 for a negative index. Its child vector is at widget +0xDC with first pointer at +0xE0 and end pointer at +0xE4, and the count is the pointer difference shifted right by 2, or 0 when the first pointer is null. A count less than the index returns 0xC0000000. Otherwise it calls 0x0052F7F0 and returns the identity of the object that the element points at, through 0x004D6750.

0x0052F7F0 calls 0x005CF390 when the vector size is not greater than the index. That routine builds the string invalid vector<T> subscript from 0x00F9D618 with length 0x1B and throws through 0x009D1B9F with throw info 0x011AA734, whose type is .?AVout_of_range@std@@. An index equal to the count passes the 0x00537C37 test and reaches that throw.
Whether the C++ exception from the index-equals-count case is caught before it leaves the Lua call.
The identity is stored through 0x00CC9320, resolved through 0x00CC7A50 and pushed through 0x00748B30. No instruction compares it with 0xC0000000 first.

The empty identity 0xC0000000 resolves to a null control and pushes Nil. 0x00CD8160 and 0x00CD81D0 return null directly only for the identity 0xE0000000 and otherwise search the containers, so the result depends on 0xC0000000 being absent from them.

rows.behavior: Passes the control identity address to 0x0075BA90, which resolves the widget through 0x004D9910 and calls 0x00533FF0. That routine returns 0 when the first pointer of the child vector at widget +0xE0 is null and otherwise the pointer difference to +0xE4 shifted right by 2. The count is pushed as an int. The callback takes no argument and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The count is read from the child vector first pointer at widget +0xE0 and end pointer at +0xE4 without a null test on the resolved widget.
The result is pushed through 0x00584F70 with the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.

arguments.handlerRead: 0x0071CE70 tag 3, or tag 6 Nil tested first
arguments.note: Container name. A Nil cell or an empty string selects the default container.

rows.behavior: The thunk jumps through receiver vftable slot +0x90. WidgetBase slot 0x00707870 requires a cell vector of at least 2 cells, reads argument 1 as a Utf8String, and tests the tag byte of cell 0. Tag 6 passes the control identity and argument 1 to 0x0075B9C0, which calls 0x00538740 with an empty container name. Any other tag reads argument 0 as a Utf8String and passes the identity and both strings to 0x0075B9E0. Both reach 0x005386D0 on the widget resolved through 0x004D9910. That routine takes the dword at widget +0x98 when the container name equals the static empty string at 0x01266B10, and otherwise the mapped dword for the name in the map at widget +0xEC, or -1 when the name is absent. It resolves a control with 0x00537950, casts the result with 0x009DA6CC from .?AVDependencyObject@Sqwt@@ to .?AVFrameworkElement@Sqwt@@ and calls slot +0x38 of the object at cast +0xB4. The AL of that call is pushed as the bool. DesktopWidget overrides slot 0x90 with 0x006DCAF0, a bare ret 4, so a DesktopWidget receiver pushes nothing. The callback requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback at 0x006DED80 is a three-instruction thunk through slot +0x90. WidgetBase vftable 0x00FD5A74 holds 0x00707870 there and DesktopWidget vftable 0x00FD5B8C holds 0x006DCAF0.
0x006DCAF0 is a bare ret 4 and pushes no value.
The WidgetBase slot checks that the cell vector has more than 1 cell, reads argument 1 through 0x0071CE70, and branches on the tag byte of cell 0 being 6.

A Nil argument 0 calls 0x0075B9C0, which calls 0x00538740, which calls 0x005386D0 with the static empty string at 0x01266B10 as the container name. A string argument 0 calls 0x0075B9E0, which calls 0x005386D0 with both strings.

0x005386D0 compares the container name with the static string through 0x00445D20. Equal strings take the dword at widget +0x98, and others take 0x005353E0. That routine searches the map at widget +0xEC and returns the dword at node +0x60 or -1.

0x005386D0 passes the control name and that value to 0x00537950, casts its result through 0x009DA6CC and calls through the table at cast +0xB4 slot +0x38. No instruction tests the cast result for null.
0x00537950 returns 0 for an empty control name, and also when 0x00535690 returns null for the container value.
The slot stores AL from the focus call and pushes it as the bool through 0x00748870.
The call through cast +0xB4 slot +0x38 is the keyboard focus request. The bytes show the call and its AL result and do not name the slot.
The lookup behind 0x00537950 and 0x00535690, the body of the Sqwt slot, and whether the Utf8String stack operator admits a Nil cell for argument 0.

rows.behavior: Reads the engine handle at ExecuteParameters +0x04, loads the dword at the 0x00CC7510 address and then the dword at +0x04 of that value. It calls 0x0075D120 with the engine handle on the object at +0x110 of that value, then calls 0x0075CE30 on the object at +0x00. The AL of the second call is pushed as the bool. 0x0075CE30 returns false when the dword at +0x508 of its context is nonzero and the byte at +0x505 is nonzero, and true otherwise. 0x0075D120 queries property 0x0007A122 of the object identified by 0xC0000024. A true result queries properties 0x0007A123 and 0x0007A121 and stores a packed dword at context +0x500 when the pair changed from the cache at +0x04 and +0x08. A false result stores 0 there when the cache byte at +0x09 is set. The pushed value does not read +0x500. The callback takes no argument and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback calls 0x0075D120 before 0x0075CE30 and pushes only the AL of the second call.
0x0075CE30 reads the dword at +0x508 through 0x004D7260 and the byte at +0x505 through 0x004D7250. It returns 0 when both are nonzero and 1 otherwise.

0x0075D120 queries 0x0007A122 first. A true result sets the byte at its +0x09, queries 0x0007A123 and 0x0007A121, and builds a dword with bit 0 set, the low 5 bits of the 0x0007A123 result in bits 1 to 5 and the low 2 bits of the 0x0007A121 result in bits 6 and 7. It stores the dword at context +0x500 through 0x004D7230 only when that pair differs from the cache at its +0x04 and +0x08. A false result stores 0 at +0x500 and clears the cache when the byte at +0x09 is set.
The only direct store encodings of the byte at +0x505 sit in a constructor body that also writes +0x4F4 through +0x50C.

The objects behind 0x004D7230, 0x004D7250 and 0x004D7260 are one state class, because they are adjacent accessors of one offset family. The two callback reads reach it through different dereference chains and their identity was not traced.
The writers of +0x505 and +0x508 after construction, the meaning of properties 0x0007A121 to 0x0007A123 and the object identified by 0xC0000024.

arguments.handlerRead: tag byte at cell +0x0C, dispatched by 0x006E8360
arguments.note: Source of the entry. 0x007422C0 builds the alternatives through 0x00740C30 and appends the Which operator through 0x00CCA2D0.
The remaining values are collected into a temporary list.

rows.behavior: Clears the byte at DesktopWidget +0x79, allocates 0xC bytes and constructs an AppendMessageResumeChecker on the widget through 0x007139C0, and requests a yield through 0x00CD2860 with the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08. It then calls the shared worker 0x006E8360 with flag 1 and returns. The worker reads arguments 1 to 3, converts argument 2 to an identity, collects the suffix, takes the sink object at +0xF8 of the second object of the state chain and dispatches on the tag of cell 0. Tag 0 calls 0x007721B0, tag 3 calls 0x00772560, and a control cell calls 0x00772650 for a WorldMaster and 0x00772050 for a CharaBase. Any other cell appends nothing. The checker poll resumes the thread once the byte at +0x79 is nonzero.

resumeChecker.poll: 0x00713A20 tests the byte at +0x79 of the widget stored at checker +0x04. A nonzero byte sets checker +0x08 to 1 and stores the dword at 0x01377ECC in the result cell. A zero byte stores the dword at 0x0130CECC. The poll of the text data checker at 0x00718640 uses the same two cells.
resumeChecker.destructor: Slot 0 at 0x00718E70 calls the body at 0x00718E10, which sets the widget byte at +0x79 to 1 at 0x00718E4C when checker +0x08 is 0.

facts.claim: The callback clears the byte at +0x79, builds the checker, requests the yield and only then calls the shared worker with flag 1.

The writers of 1 to the byte at +0x79 in DesktopWidget code are the constructor at 0x006E06A9, where AL holds 1, the method 0x006DCA80 and the checker destructor at 0x00718E4C. The method is called from 0x0057596B after the identity 0xC0000024 resolves through 0x00CC7A50. A scan of byte-store encodings also finds stores to +0x79 at 0x004718AC and from 0x007EA7A5 on. They lie in other regions and were not attributed.

The worker reads index 0 as a tag byte, index 1 as an int, index 2 through 0x0071BB80 and index 3 as an int, and collects index 4 onward through 0x007702C0. It loads the sink object from +0xF8 of the second object of the state chain.

The tag 0 path passes the int, argument 1, the identity address, argument 3, the collected list and the flag to 0x007721B0. The tag 3 path reads index 0 through 0x0071D770 and calls 0x00772560. The tag 4 path reads index 0 through 0x0071CCF0, casts to .?AVWorldMaster@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@ and calls 0x00772650, otherwise casts to .?AVCharaBase@Control@Client@Script@Lua@Application@@ and calls 0x00772050. A control that passes neither cast appends nothing.

0x007721B0 builds a record through 0x0076B3D0, stores its first argument at record +0x108, allocates 0x48 bytes for a second object through 0x00789CD0 and hands it to the object at +0xE0 of the second chain object through 0x00770F10. It ends with 0x00770C00 on the sink.

The yield holds the Lua thread until a later store of 1 to the +0x79 byte. That the store marks the end of the message display is inferred from the clear before the yield and the three writers found. No consumer of the message path was traced.

The bodies of 0x00772560, 0x00772650 and 0x00772050, the lifetime of the pool record, the caller of the function around 0x0057596B, and whether the yield takes effect before or after the worker returns to the dispatcher.

arguments.handlerRead: tag byte at cell +0x0C, dispatched by 0x006E8360
arguments.note: Source of the entry, the same list as _appendMessagePool.

rows.behavior: Calls the shared worker 0x006E8360 with flag 0 and returns. The argument list, the worker and the sink dispatch are those of _appendMessagePool. This callback clears no byte, builds no checker and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the four instructions that push flag 0 and the ExecuteParameters reference and call 0x006E8360.
The argument list builder 0x00743A30 is shared with _appendMessagePool and appends 5 entries in the order of the arguments above.

notFunctorNatives.note: Listed by xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json with 179 call sites and no binding. xivl-decomp:docs/script/lua-bootstrap-chunks.md records _math as a value namespace for math. The literal at 0x00FE0850 is referenced once from 0x0078FD3C and has no registrar of the 0x00CCCAD0 shape among the rows here.

xivl-decomp:docs/script/widget-work-members.md records it as a work declaration key. Its literal at 0x0110F6BC has no direct code reference. The only reference found is the dword pointer at 0x0130D84C in .data, loaded at 0x00D212A8 by the helper at 0x00D212A0 and left untraced.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The functions that contain those call sites were not traced, so the run-time order of registration is not established.
Script call-site lines are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given widget instance reaches at run time.
No NpcSayWidget call to the rows here is recorded. The tracked metadata lists only _defineClass for that script.
The _inl descriptor to _cpp name mapping and the receiverless Global mapping were not traced.
The type mismatch route through 0x00CCA730 is recorded up to the call of 0x00CF38A0. Whether that call returns to the handler is unknown.
Faults and C++ exceptions raised inside a callback were not followed past the callback.
The pool sinks, the Sqwt focus slot, the widget lookup behind 0x00537950 and the writers of widget +0xD8 were not traced.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish message text, widget layout or server behavior.
